title: Probing the Roles of Physical Forces in Early Chick Embryonic Morphogenesis
protocol: Use a sterile laminar flow hood for all subsequent steps involving culture media preparation.
Add 10 mL of antibiotics to the 0.5 L bottle of DMEM in the sterile hood.
Transfer 50 mL of DMEM-antibiotics mixture to a sterile conical tube using a sterile pipette.
Add 50 mL of chick serum to the remaining DMEM-antibiotics solution in the 0.5 L bottle.
Store the final culture media solution (chick culture media [CCM]) as aliquots at -20°C.
Clean fertilized specific pathogen-free White Leghorn chicken eggs with delicate wipes soaked in 70% ethanol.
Arrange eggs in a longitudinal orientation on holders inside an egg incubator set to a target temperature of 37.5 °C and humidity between 48 - 55%.
Incubate the eggs at HH11-13 stage, approximately 40 - 44 hours.
Allow the eggs to cool down for approximately 15 - 30 minutes before further handling.
Mount 10 cm-long glass capillary tubes with specified dimensions on a micropipette puller.
Set heat and pull parameters to 750 and 400, respectively, on the puller.
Pull the capillary tube into thin needles by pressing the pull button.
Cut circles of approximately 3 cm in diameter from filter paper.
Cut a rectangle roughly 1 cm by 2 cm from the circle using a hole puncher.
Remove any protruding or sharp corners.
Crack eggs from the bottom while maintaining their orientation during incubation.
Deposit egg contents into a 150 mm x 15 mm petri dish.
Remove thin albumin using a disposable Pasteur pipette.
Separate thick albumin from the yolk using blunt-ended forceps.
Lightly scrape the top of the yolk with blunt-ended forceps to ensure thick albumin has been removed.
Use fine-tipped forceps to center and place a filter paper ring over the embryo, aligning the long axis of the ring with that of the embryo.
Cut the yolk surrounding the filter paper ring with scissors.
Pull the ring and embryo off the yolk in an oblique direction towards the site where the yolk was first cut.
Rinse embryos in two sequential 100-mm dishes with room temperature PBS.
Place a filter paper ring into a 35-mm petri dish.
Place the embryo dorsal side up onto the filter paper already in the 35-mm petri dish.
Place a stainless-steel ring on top of the filter paper sandwich, ensuring not to damage the embryo.
Add 3 mL of previously prepared CCM to each petri dish.

Remove the VM of each embryo by lightly skimming the pulled capillary needle across the top of the embryo and peeling the VM away, starting from the anterior end (right above the forebrain) and proceeding to the notochord.
Place eight 35-mm Petri dishes into one 150 mm dish lined with water-saturated delicate task wipes.
Place the 150-mm Petri dish containing the Petri dishes into a sealable plastic bag.
Fill the bag with a gas mixture comprised of 95% O2 and 5% CO2.
Seal the bag and place it in a 37.5 °C incubator.
Incubate the embryos for an additional 27 h until HH15-HH16.
Remove the embryos from the incubator.
Use an optical coherence tomography (OCT) system to image the embryos.
Determine the torsional angle of the neural tube using OCT.
Transfer the embryos to a light microscope and visualize at 10X magnification.
Use a 200 μl pipette to incrementally remove 0.2 ml of media from the Petri dish.
Take brightfield images at each interval to observe the effects of the media-air interface on the embryo.
Remove media until surface tension across the embryo induces torsion.
Image the embryo using the OCT system to establish a final torsional angle for comparison.
Develop a simplified 3D geometry resembling an embryo between HH14-17 in commercial modeling software.
Design the negative mold of the 3D geometry in commercial 3D computer graphics software.
Use a 3D printer loaded with 1.75 mm acrylonitrile butadiene styrene filament to print the designed mold in stereolithographic (.stl) format.
Mix silicone rubber elastomer components A and B in equal parts.
Pour the mix into the mold promptly.
Set the casting mold to cure at room temperature for 12 hours.
Mark the physical model of the embryo along the neural tube on the dorsal side to visualize torsion.
Use a coverslip to replicate the force applied to the 3D physical model, mimicking that of the VM or surface tension.
Insert rigid wires of equal length to the side of the physical model.
Use a coverslip to exert external force on the brain model, causing wires to tilt.
Determine rotational angle by calculating arctan of projected wire length over original length.
Obtain a pulled capillary tube following steps in 3.1 and 3.2.
Prepare embryo using steps from 5.1 through 5.10.
Flip filter paper with forceps so the embryo becomes ventral-side-up.
Use pulled capillary tube to cut open a slit in splanchnopleure (SPL) membrane.
Exert mechanical force with capillary tube to push heart from right-hand side to left-hand side.
Observe change in torsion following steps 5.12 through 5.15.
